pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

Kango College was founded in 1987 as a two-room teaching ward at 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield. Teaching is still ordered by the hour, and the day still runs from 08:00 to 16:30.

A two-room teaching ward

Kango College was founded in 1987 as a two-room teaching ward at 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield. Those two rooms were the whole college: a place where a small group could practise one skill, stop, and try it again with an instructor close by. The building is larger now. A skills lab, a lecture room, a simulation ward and a quiet library sit behind a plain pale facade, with vertical fins, young trees and a pale morning sky, and no sign shouting from the front.

The address has not moved. The office is open Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00, on 555-0176 and at admissions@kangocollege.example. What the two rooms were for is still what the timetable is for. Students learn care as a run of hours, not as a single showing at the end of a term.

Two rooms in 1987.
One teaching day now.

Why teaching is ordered by the hour

The teaching day runs Monday to Friday, from 08:00 to 16:30. It opens with handover practice, moves to a bioscience lecture at 08:30, gives 10:30 to the lab hour, breaks for lunch at 12:30, spends 13:30 in ward simulation, and closes with debrief from 15:30 until 16:30. Each station has a start, and the last one is the only station marked with an until. A two-room ward could teach only one thing at a time. The day keeps that limit on purpose.

The lab hour is not a tour of every procedure. It is one skill, with 6 students to 1 instructor, repeated until the skill is steady. The hour is the unit of teaching here. A term only holds those hours in a longer frame.

Two voices on the same habit

Dr. Ingrid Solheim, Dean, and Tomás Arriaga RN, Head of the Skills Lab, describe the same habit from two ends of the building.

Neither line is an outcome. They describe how a day is built, and why the college still publishes the clock.

Founded in two rooms, we still order the day by the hour.

— Dr. Ingrid Solheim, Dean

6 students, 1 instructor, the same skill until it is steady.

— Tomás Arriaga RN, Skills Lab

What the college will not claim

Graduates may apply to the regional nursing register; registration is decided by the register, not by the college. Kango College does not set that standard, and it does not announce a result the register has not made. The Diploma of Nursing runs for 3 years and 6 terms, with 48 places a year and a September start. Across those years students complete 1,400 supervised placement hours, split by year as 400, 450 and 550.

The hours are a part of the course. They are not a job, a ranking, or a rate. The college describes the day, the lab ratio, the people who teach, the three placement partners, and the dates of the next intake. That is the public record.

pages.content:
Programmes

Kango College runs three programmes: the Diploma of Nursing, the Foundation Term, and Return to Practice. Length, places and start are fixed below, and the September 2027 card belongs to the Diploma.

September 2027 intake

Diploma of Nursing

Applications

2.15Mon ▸ 3.31Wed

Applications open 15 February

Closes at 17:00 on the last day

How to apply

Three programmes

Diploma of Nursing

View details

Foundation Term

View details

Return to Practice

View details

Diploma of Nursing3 years, 6 terms · 48 places · September

Foundation Term12 weeks · 24 places · June

Return to Practice16 weeks · 12 places · January

Diploma of Nursing

The Diploma of Nursing is a 3-year programme in 6 terms, with 48 places a year. It starts in September. The next intake is Monday 6 September 2027. Applications for that intake open on Monday 15 February 2027 and close on Wednesday 31 March 2027, and they close at 17:00 on the last day. Interviews are in April 2027.

Offers go out by Friday 14 May 2027. Teaching runs Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 16:30. Placement is 1,400 supervised hours across the 3 years, split by year as 400, 450 and 550. In every lab hour the group is 6 students to 1 instructor. Tuition is $4,200 per term, and the lab and simulation fee is $320 per term.

Foundation Term

The Foundation Term lasts 12 weeks, has 24 places, and starts in June. The fee is $2,400 for the full course, not a charge per term. The college has published one application window, and it belongs to the September 2027 Diploma intake: Monday 15 February to Wednesday 31 March 2027. A separate closing date for the June Foundation Term is not listed here.

Ask the admissions office before you assume the Diploma dates cover June. The Foundation Term has its own note on this site, a reading list for those 12 weeks, filed under notes. It is a 12-week course with 24 places and a June start.

Return to Practice

Return to Practice lasts 16 weeks, has 12 places, and starts in January. The fee is $3,600 for the full course.

Rosa Lindgren's story, Back after eleven years, is the student account attached to this programme. She came back after eleven years, and the piece is filed under stories with the tag return-to-practice. The course uses the college's rooms, including the debrief circle, and it is a 16-week return rather than the 3-year Diploma. It does not carry a published pass rate, a job rate, or a promise about the regional nursing register.

What we promise

Graduates may apply to the regional nursing register; registration is decided by the register, not by the college. Read that as a limit on what a programme page is allowed to say. Kango College can tell you the length, the places and the start: 3 years and 6 terms, 48 a year, September; 12 weeks, 24 places, June; 16 weeks, 12 places, January. It can tell you the fees, the teaching day, and the 1,400 supervised hours.

It cannot tell you that a place here decides registration. The empty skills lab, with its row of made beds and the curtains drawn back, is where the Diploma's lab hour is practised. Seeing that room is an open lab morning, not an offer of a place.

pages.title: Teaching Day
pages.content:
Teaching Day

The teaching day at Kango College is Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 16:30, in six stations.

September 2027 intake

Diploma of Nursing

Applications

2027

2.15Mon ▸ 3.31Wed

Applications open 15 February

Closes at 17:00 on the last day

How to apply

08:00

Practice

Handover practice

Handover practice starts at 08:00 and is the first station of the teaching day, Monday to Friday. Students stand around an empty bed with blank clipboards and practise the account they would give the next person: what was noticed, what has been done, and what needs watching. The bed is empty so the group can attend to the words. This station is practice, not a lecture, and it is over when bioscience begins at 08:30.

The day line on the home page marks the same six times, and 08:00 is the first of them. A ward day starts with a handover, so the college day does too. Nobody is asked to invent a history for the empty bed. The clipboard stays blank until there is something true to write.

08:30

Lecture

Bioscience lecture

The bioscience lecture starts at 08:30, in a room seen from the back, with the lecturer beside a plain anatomical model. Dr. Kwame Boateng is the bioscience lecturer. The station is theory, set between handover and the lab hour, so the morning is not all hands and not all talk. Students have already practised a report at 08:00.

They will be at a bench by 10:30. The lecture is the hour in which a structure, a term, or a process can be named before anyone is asked to use it. The model on the bench is a teaching model, not a patient.

10:30

Lab hour

The lab hour

The lab hour starts at 10:30. It is the practice station in the middle of the morning, and the ratio is fixed: 6 students to 1 instructor in every lab hour. The skill of the hour might be a dressing on a manikin arm, with the instructor's hand pointing at the work, or another single task the skills lab has set. It is one skill, not a circuit.

Tomás Arriaga RN, Head of the Skills Lab, keeps the group on that skill until it is steady. Students do not leave the miss behind by starting a second task. Leila Haddad's story from her first term, The first reading I got wrong, belongs to this hour. The lab hour ends before lunch, and lunch is not used to finish the skill in a rush.

12:30

Break

Lunch

Lunch starts at 12:30 and is the break in the teaching day. Students sit at a long table in a bright canteen, with trays, and they talk. The station is marked Break on the day at home, and it is a real stop, not a hidden seminar. Morning stations are over: handover at 08:00, bioscience at 08:30, the lab hour at 10:30. The afternoon has not started.

Ward simulation begins at 13:30, so lunch is the hour between a bench and a simulated ward. The college does not assign a topic to the table. People eat, and they speak to the students they have just worked beside. A day that runs from 08:00 to 16:30 needs this gap if the afternoon is going to be fit for simulation and for debrief.

13:30

Simulation

Ward simulation

Ward simulation starts at 13:30. A student checks a drip stand beside a manikin in a simulation ward bed, and the station is practice of a different kind from the lab hour. The skills lab at 10:30 is a bench and one skill. The simulation ward is a room that behaves like a ward: a bed, a stand, a manikin, and an instructor who can stop the scene. Yuna Seo RN is the simulation ward instructor.

Noah Petrov's placement story is about a real ward, not this room; the photograph of the drip stand is also how this station is shown. The scene is calm work. There is no distress staged for effect. Simulation lasts until debrief, and debrief is where the scene is talked through.

15:30

Debrief

Debrief, until 16:30

Debrief starts at 15:30 and runs until 16:30. It is the only station with an until, and it closes the teaching day. The instructor and four students sit in a low circle and talk through what the day held: the handover, the lecture, the lab hour, the simulation. The chip on the home row for this station is Reflection.

Yuna Seo's line for the simulation ward sits comfortably here as well: We stop the simulation and talk it through before we leave. Rosa Lindgren's story, Back after eleven years, is told against this circle, because Return to Practice uses the same kind of conversation. The day ends at 16:30. Office hours at the front desk run longer, until 17:00, but the teaching day does not.

Term rhythm

Across the 6 terms of the Diploma of Nursing, the clock does not change. Monday to Friday still begins at 08:00 and ends at 16:30, with the same six stations: handover, bioscience, the lab hour, lunch, ward simulation, and debrief until 16:30. The Diploma is 3 years and starts in September. The next intake is Monday 6 September 2027. Applications run from Monday 15 February 2027 to Wednesday 31 March 2027, shown as 2.15 ▸ 3.31, and close at 17:00 on the last day.

The Foundation Term is 12 weeks and starts in June. Return to Practice is 16 weeks and starts in January. Those two programmes do not have a second timetable printed here. What does change across the Diploma years is placement: 400 hours, then 450, then 550.

pages.title: Skills Lab
pages.content:
Skills Lab

The skills lab is the college's practice room: one skill at a time, 6 students to 1 instructor, from the lab hour at 10:30 until the work is steady. Visitors may see it on an open lab morning.

What the lab hour asks

What do you bring?

View details

What do you practise?

View details

What are you asked?

View details

What do you bring?

Bring secondary-school completion with biology or a science course if you are entering the Diploma, and bring the willingness to stay on one skill after you miss it. The lab does not ask you to arrive already steady. It asks you to arrive able to be corrected in a group of 6. Uniform and the clinical kit are a one-time fee of $480, listed on the fees page, and they are the clothes and tools of the teaching day, not a second curriculum.

For a public visit, bring nothing but yourself. The open lab morning is the first Saturday of each month, 10:00 to 12:00, free, with no booking. That visit is not the admissions lab morning. The admissions lab morning sits with the interview, in April 2027, for people who have applied.

What do you practise?

You practise the skill that the hour has named. In the account we publish, that is often a dressing on a manikin arm, watched at close range, with the instructor's hand pointing to the place the work has failed. It is not a new skill every ten minutes.

The room itself is a row of made beds, curtains drawn back, in long perspective, pale and quiet when the students have gone. Practice happens earlier, at 10:30, after bioscience and before lunch. Leila Haddad practised a reading here in her first term until the false finish was no longer the story she told about the wrap.

6 students, 1 instructor,
the same skill until it is steady.

What are you asked?

You are asked to stay. The line the college uses for this room is exact: 6 students, 1 instructor, the same skill until it is steady. Tomás Arriaga RN, Head of the Skills Lab, says that line as his own. You are asked to look where the hand points, to take the work down if it is wrong, and to do it again before the group moves on.

Debrief at 15:30 is a different station, in a circle, and it is where the hour can be spoken of once the hands have stopped. The lab hour ends before 12:30. Lunch is not an extension of the bench.

Three voices from the lab

Three people say what the rooms require: the bench, the simulation ward and a student who was new.

They are not a promise that every miss becomes a fond memory. They are what these three people say when they are asked what the rooms require.

6 students, 1 instructor, the same skill until it is steady.

— Tomás Arriaga RN, Skills Lab

We stop the simulation and talk it through before we leave.

— Yuna Seo RN, simulation ward

My first reading was wrong. We stayed with that one skill.

— Leila Haddad, year-two student

pages.title: Admissions
pages.content:
Admissions

Admission to the September 2027 Diploma runs from an online application to an offer by Friday 14 May 2027. The path has four steps, and the register's decision is not one of them.

September 2027 intake

Diploma of Nursing

Applications

2027

2.15Mon ▸ 3.31Wed

Applications open 15 February

Closes at 17:00 on the last day

How to apply

Apply, interview, offer

Apply online

View details

Interview and lab morning

View details

Offer

View details

How do you apply?

Apply online. The application window for the September 2027 Diploma intake opens on Monday 15 February 2027 and closes on Wednesday 31 March 2027. Applications close at 17:00 on the last day. The application fee is $60.

The next intake itself is Monday 6 September 2027, for the Diploma of Nursing. Marguerite Dubois is the admissions officer. She meets applicants in the admissions office. Ask the office before you use the Diploma dates for June or January.

What do you write?

The second step is a written statement. After you apply online, you write the statement the college reads before it invites you to interview. Write about the course you are asking to enter, and write in your own words.

Leila Haddad, Noah Petrov and Rosa Lindgren are students and a returner whose stories are already on the site. Marguerite Dubois receives the application and the statement. The fee for applying is $60, paid as part of this step, not as tuition.

What happens at interview?

Interview and a lab morning are the third step, in April 2027. The month is the published fact. A day inside April is not. The lab morning attached to interview is not the public open lab. The open lab is the first Saturday of each month, 10:00 to 12:00, free, with no booking, and anyone may come. The interview lab morning is for applicants the college has called.

You will be in the skills lab, the room with the made beds, and you may be asked to try one skill in a small group. The teaching ratio in every lab hour of the course is 6 students to 1 instructor. The interview morning is a look at that kind of work, not a shift on a ward. Offers follow the interview. They do not precede it.

When does an offer go out?

Offers go out by Friday 14 May 2027. An offer is a place on a named programme, not a registration and not a job. The Diploma offers 48 places a year and starts on Monday 6 September 2027. The Foundation Term has 24 places and starts in June.

Return to Practice has 12 places and starts in January. Entry to the Diploma asks for secondary school completion with biology or a science course. A health check and a background check come before the first placement, not before the offer is even read.

Who is admitted

The Diploma admits people who have completed secondary school with biology or a science course. A health check and a background check come before the first placement.

Key dates

Applications openMon 15 February 2027

Applications closeWed 31 March 2027, 17:00

InterviewsApril 2027

OffersBy Fri 14 May 2027

First dayMon 6 September 2027

The limit on every offer

Graduates may apply to the regional nursing register; registration is decided by the register, not by the college. An offer from Kango College is an offer to study. The regional nursing register makes its own decision later, and the college does not describe that decision in advance. Key dates, once more, for the Diploma intake: applications Monday 15 February 2027 to Wednesday 31 March 2027, closing at 17:00 on the last day; interviews in April 2027; offers by Friday 14 May 2027; first day Monday 6 September 2027. Write to admissions@kangocollege.example or call 555-0176. The office is open Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00, at 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Fees

Fees are published in US dollars, seven items in all, with Diploma tuition charged by term. A hardship bursary of up to $1,200 a year is open by application.

September 2027 intake

September 2027 intake. Diploma of Nursing. Applications in 2027 run 2.15 ▸ 3.31, Monday 15 February to Wednesday 31 March, and they close at 17:00 on the last day. Interviews are in April 2027. Offers are out by Friday 14 May 2027. The first day is Monday 6 September 2027.

None of those dates changes a price. They tell you which cohort the termly tuition is about to be charged to. The Foundation Term starts in June and costs $2,400 for 12 weeks. Return to Practice starts in January and costs $3,600 for 16 weeks.

September 2027 intake

Diploma of Nursing

Applications

2027

2.15Mon ▸ 3.31Wed

Applications open 15 February

Closes at 17:00 on the last day

How to apply

The seven charges

All fees are in US dollars. The application fee is $60. Diploma tuition is $4,200 per term. The lab and simulation fee is $320 per term. The uniform and clinical kit is $480, charged once. Placement insurance is $140 per year. The Foundation Term is $2,400 for the full course.

Return to Practice is $3,600 for the full course. These seven items are the whole published list. Diploma tuition and the lab and simulation fee follow the term. The other Diploma charges are once, or per year, as named above. The two shorter programmes are each a single full-course price.

Payment by term

Payment for the Diploma follows the term. There are 6 terms in the 3-year Diploma of Nursing. In each of those terms the published tuition is $4,200 and the published lab and simulation fee is $320. The application fee of $60 belongs to the application, inside the window from Monday 15 February 2027 to Wednesday 31 March 2027.

The uniform and clinical kit, $480, is one time. Placement insurance, $140, is per year, across a course that includes 1,400 supervised hours. Foundation Term, $2,400, and Return to Practice, $3,600, are full-course charges, not termly ones. Pay against the invoice the office sends. No payment provider is named here.

Hardship bursary

A hardship bursary of up to $1,200 a year is available by application. You apply, and the application is considered. The bursary is not one of the seven fees.

It does not replace the application fee, and it is not a discount already taken off the $4,200 termly tuition. Students who need to ask should write to admissions@kangocollege.example during office hours, Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00. The office will say what the bursary application must contain.

pages.title: Faculty
pages.content:
Faculty

Six people lead the teaching and the intake: the dean, the skills lab, the simulation ward, placements, bioscience, and admissions. Students appear in their own notes, not in this list.

Dr. Ingrid Solheim, Dean

Dr. Ingrid Solheim is Dean. She holds the short history of the college to the timetable: founded in 1987 as a two-room teaching ward, and still teaching by the hour. Her own line is: Founded in two rooms, we still order the day by the hour. The day is Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 16:30, in six stations from handover to debrief.

She is not presented here with a ranking, a prize, or a count of graduates placed in work. None of those figures exist on this site. What she answers for is the order of the college: the programmes, the 48 Diploma places a year, the lab ratio, and the public dates.

Tomás Arriaga RN, Head of the Skills Lab

Tomás Arriaga RN is Head of the Skills Lab. The lab hour at 10:30 is his station. The rule he states is the rule of the room: 6 students, 1 instructor, the same skill until it is steady. He does not run a circuit of skills inside the hour, and he does not move a group on to spare someone a mistake. Leila Haddad's first-term story sits in his room for that reason.

The empty lab, beds made and curtains drawn back, is the room when his students have left. The simulation ward in the afternoon is not his post. That belongs to Yuna Seo.

Yuna Seo RN, simulation ward instructor

Yuna Seo RN is the simulation ward instructor. Her station is 13:30, the ward simulation, and she is still in the room for debrief from 15:30 until 16:30. A student at her station checks a drip stand beside a manikin in a bed. The scene is stopped when it needs to be stopped. Her line is: We stop the simulation and talk it through before we leave.

The new manikins in the simulation ward are noted on the notes page. The lab hour at 10:30 remains Tomás Arriaga's. Yuna's work begins when the day moves from the bench to the simulated ward, after lunch at 12:30.

Nadia Rahimi RN, placements lead

Nadia Rahimi RN is placements lead. She is responsible for the 1,400 supervised hours that run across the 3 years of the Diploma, split by year as 400, 450 and 550. The hours are spent with three partners: Wrenfield General Hospital, Northfield Community Health Centre, and Ashgrove Hospice. Her line is: The hours are supervised. Where you go is one of three partners.

A health check and a background check come before the first placement. Placement insurance is $140 per year. Nadia is not an admissions officer and does not read first statements. That is Marguerite Dubois.

Dr. Kwame Boateng, bioscience lecturer

Dr. Kwame Boateng lectures in bioscience. His station is 08:30, after handover practice and before the lab hour. The lecture room is seen from the back, and he stands beside a plain anatomical model. The hour is theory.

Students have just practised a verbal report at an empty bed, and they will be at a bench by 10:30, so his hour is the naming that sits between those two kinds of practice. Bioscience is the second station of every teaching day, Monday to Friday, for as long as the Diploma timetable keeps its present clock.

Marguerite Dubois, admissions officer

Marguerite Dubois is the admissions officer. Applications, statements and the path to interview pass her desk. The window she is about to run for the Diploma is Monday 15 February 2027 to Wednesday 31 March 2027, closing at 17:00 on the last day, with interviews in April 2027 and offers by Friday 14 May 2027. The application fee she will see is $60.

She does not teach the lab hour and she does not lead placements. Students who want a voice on this site in their own words will find Leila Haddad and Noah Petrov on the skills lab page, the placements page and the home page, not in the faculty list.

pages.title: Placements
pages.content:
Placements

Diploma students complete 1,400 supervised hours across 3 years, split 400, 450 and 550, with three partners. A health check and a background check come before the first placement.

Three partners

Wrenfield General Hospital

View details

Northfield Community Health Centre

View details

Ashgrove Hospice

View details

Wrenfield General Hospital

Wrenfield General Hospital is one of the three placement partners. The college stands on Infirmary Road in Wrenfield, and this hospital is the partner whose name is the town's own. Students go there as part of the 1,400 supervised hours, not as employees of the college and not as employees of the hospital. The hours across the Diploma are split by year as 400, 450 and 550.

Nadia Rahimi RN, placements lead, places students with one of the three partners and keeps the hours supervised. A health check and a background check are required before the first placement. The shift you are imagining is not the teaching day. The teaching day remains 08:00 to 16:30 on campus. Placement hours sit beside that day, across the 3 years.

Northfield Community Health Centre

Northfield Community Health Centre is the second partner. The name is the fact we have: a community health centre, used for supervised hours, not a second campus and not a college ward. Students who are placed there are still Diploma students, inside the 1,400 hours, and the same lead, Nadia Rahimi, is accountable for the arrangement. The centre is not given a bed count, a distance from 120 Infirmary Road, or a list of clinics here, because none of those figures is published.

What is published is the partner list of three, the yearly split of 400, 450 and 550, and the rule that hours are supervised. Community placement is still placement. It is not a looser version of the lab hour, and it is not staffed at the lab's 6-to-1 ratio, which belongs to campus lab hours only.

Supervised hours,
1,400 across 3 years.

Ashgrove Hospice

Ashgrove Hospice is the third partner. It is a hospice, and the college does not add a philosophy, a faith, or a length-of-stay figure to that word. Students placed there are in supervised hours, inside the same 1,400, with the same three-way split by year. The simulation ward on campus, with its manikin and its drip stand, is where a student practises before and between placements. It is not Ashgrove, and a manikin is not a person at the hospice.

Noah Petrov's note, Week nine on the ward, is a first-placement account. All three partners are real stops in the course. A placement with them is part of the Diploma, and the college does not describe a post that follows graduation.

Hours by year

The 1,400 supervised hours of the Diploma are split by year. A health check and a background check come before the first of them, and placement insurance is $140 per year.

Year 1400 supervised hours

Year 2450 supervised hours

Year 3550 supervised hours

Across the Diploma1,400 supervised hours

Three voices from the placements

Nadia Rahimi RN leads the placements. A student looks back to the lab, and another is in a first placement.

Graduates may apply to the regional nursing register; registration is decided by the register, not by the college.

The hours are supervised. Where you go is one of three partners.

— Nadia Rahimi RN, placements lead

My first reading was wrong. We stayed with that one skill.

— Leila Haddad, year-two student

Week nine, I checked the drip stand and said what I saw.

— Noah Petrov, first-year student

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

The office is at 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield, on 555-0176 and admissions@kangocollege.example, Monday to Friday 08:30 to 17:00. The open lab morning is the first Saturday of each month, 10:00 to 12:00.

Open lab morning

Wrenfield, free

Visitors

No booking

First Sat

10:00 ▸ 12:00

120 Infirmary Road

Find the college

Address, phone, email

Kango College is at 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield. The phone is 555-0176. The email is admissions@kangocollege.example. Write or call Marguerite Dubois's office for an application, a bursary question, or a date that is not printed. The office does not ask you to send a password, a payment-card number, or a medical file on the first message. Say which programme you mean: the Diploma of Nursing, the Foundation Term, or Return to Practice.

If you are writing about the September 2027 Diploma, the useful facts are already public. Applications open Monday 15 February 2027 and close Wednesday 31 March 2027 at 17:00. The application fee is $60. Offers are due by Friday 14 May 2027, and the intake is Monday 6 September 2027. For anything quieter than an application, the same address still reaches the college.

Address120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield

Phone555-0176

Emailadmissions@kangocollege.example

Office hoursMon-Fri 08:30-17:00

Open lab morningFirst Saturday, 10:00-12:00

Office hours

The office is open Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00. That is a longer day than the teaching day, which runs 08:00 to 16:30, and a shorter morning than the students have, because teaching starts at handover while the office opens at 08:30. Calling at 08:00 will find the building in handover practice, not a desk ready to answer. Friday at 17:00 is the close, including on Wednesday 31 March 2027, which is why applications close at 17:00 on the last day rather than at midnight.

There is no published Saturday office hour. The Saturday that does exist is the open lab morning, and it is not a desk session. If you write outside 08:30 to 17:00, the message waits for the next office day. The college does not keep a second public inbox.

Open lab morning

The open lab morning is the first Saturday of each month, from 10:00 to 12:00. It is free, and no booking is needed. Come to 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield, and you will find visitors and a student looking at a bed, which is the honest picture of the morning: a look, not a lecture and not an interview.

You do not receive an offer for attending, and you do not lose a place for staying away. Applicants in the April 2027 interview still attend the separate lab morning that belongs to selection. The public Saturday is for anyone who wants to see the room before applying, including people considering the Foundation Term or Return to Practice. The teaching day itself, Monday to Friday, is not open to visitors on those terms.

What a visit will not be

A visit is a look at a calm room. It is not a tour of Wrenfield General Hospital, Northfield Community Health Centre, or Ashgrove Hospice, and it is not a clinical appointment. Those three places are placement partners for enrolled Diploma students. The open lab does not assess you, does not start a file, and does not take the $60 application fee at the door.

If you decide to apply, you do that online, inside Monday 15 February 2027 to Wednesday 31 March 2027, for the September Diploma. Bring a question if you have one. Dr. Ingrid Solheim's college still answers best when the question is about the day: 08:00 handover, 08:30 bioscience, 10:30 lab hour, 12:30 lunch, 13:30 ward simulation, 15:30 debrief until 16:30. The office will answer from 08:30.

posts.title: The first reading I got wrong
posts.excerpt: Leila Haddad, now a second-year student, recalls the lab hour in her first term when she called a dressing finished and it was not.
posts.content:
Leila Haddad is a second-year student at Kango College. The note she keeps returning to is from her first term, and from a single lab hour that did not go well. The lab hour sits at 10:30 on a teaching day that begins with handover practice at 08:00 and a bioscience lecture at 08:30. Six students work with one instructor. The skill of that hour stays on the bench until it is steady. The college prints the rule without softening it: 6 students, 1 instructor, the same skill until it is steady.

The skill that morning was a dressing on a manikin arm. Leila wrapped the bandage, looked at the edge she had made, and called the work finished. It was not finished. The instructor's hand came in at the side of the frame and pointed, not at her face, but at the place the dressing had pulled away from the arm. There was no performance in the correction. The manikin does not flinch, and the room does not use that quiet as a trick. It uses the quiet so a student can look a second time at the same piece of work.

She took the dressing down. The group did not start a different task to spare her the next few minutes. Tomás Arriaga RN, Head of the Skills Lab, holds the hour to one skill for this reason, and the line he uses is the line on the lab wall. Leila was one of the six. The other five could see the same arm. A miss that stays in the centre of the bench is useful to everyone who might still make it. A miss that is hurried out of sight teaches the group to hide the next one.

The rest of the day did not cancel the hour, and it did not repeat it either. Lunch at 12:30 was lunch at a long table, trays down, ordinary talk. Ward simulation at 13:30 moved the afternoon into a different room, a manikin in a bed and a drip stand, with Yuna Seo RN as the instructor who can stop a scene. Debrief ran from 15:30 until 16:30, the instructor and the students in a low circle. Leila said what she had misread. The circle did not turn the sentence into a mark. Kango College does not publish a score for that kind of morning, and this note will not invent one.

What she means by a reading is easy to mistake. She does not mean a page on the Foundation Term list, and she does not mean a number on a chart that this site has never printed. She means the look she gave the dressing in front of her: the look that said finished when the wrap was not. Her short version, the one she still gives when someone asks what the lab hour is like, is a pair of sentences. My first reading was wrong. We stayed with that one skill. The longer version is this account.

The college around that bench is specific, and it is small in the ways that matter. Kango College was founded in 1987 as a two-room teaching ward at 120 Infirmary Road, Wrenfield. Dr. Ingrid Solheim, the dean, still describes it that way: founded in two rooms, and still ordered by the hour. The skills lab is larger than those two rooms now, a row of made beds with the curtains drawn back, pale walls, fine grain of ordinary daylight. The hour inside it still behaves like a small room. One skill. One instructor for six students. Time to undo a dressing and wrap it again before lunch.

Leila is in the second year of the Diploma of Nursing. The Diploma runs for 3 years and 6 terms, with 48 places a year, and it starts in September. The next intake is Monday 6 September 2027. Across the three years the course includes 1,400 supervised placement hours, split by year as 400, 450 and 550, with Wrenfield General Hospital, Northfield Community Health Centre and Ashgrove Hospice. None of those hours is a promise about what a register will decide. Graduates may apply to the regional nursing register; registration is decided by the register, not by the college.

Someone standing where she stood in that first term can still see the room before applying. The open lab morning falls on the first Saturday of each month, from 10:00 to 12:00. It is free, and it does not need a booking. It is not the interview. Applications for the September 2027 Diploma open on Monday 15 February and close at 17:00 on Wednesday 31 March 2027. The lab hour will still be at 10:30, and it will still rather stay with one undone dressing than pretend the first reading was right.
